skill.name: idor-testing
skill.description: Guide authorized IDOR assessments across web endpoints, object references, files, and access-control boundaries.
skill.summary: Test object-level authorization with controlled accounts and document evidence, impact, and remediation.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: All 65 external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code delimiters, not executable shell or Ruby syntax. One low-risk enumeration instruction is confirmed. Destructive cross-account testing and rate-limit evasion create additional medium-risk misuse potential despite the authorization warnings.

remediation.issue: Examples modify another account's resources to verify authorization failures.
remediation.suggestion: Require isolated test tenants, synthetic records, written scope, rollback steps, and non-destructive checks before any state-changing request.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance recommends IP rotation and off-peak activity to bypass rate limits.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion guidance. Require coordinated rate-limit exceptions, fixed request budgets, monitoring, and immediate termination when scope controls activate.

content.value_statement: Object references can expose or modify another user's resources when authorization checks fail. This skill structures authorized testing, evidence collection, impact analysis, and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Identifies object references in URLs, query parameters, request bodies, and file paths.
Compares resource access across controlled user accounts to detect horizontal authorization failures.
Tests alternate identifiers and HTTP methods with an intercepting proxy.
Guides Burp Suite Intruder configuration for scoped identifier testing.
Interprets status codes, response content, ownership markers, and timing differences.
Provides Django examples for ownership checks and authenticated-user filtering.
limitations: The skill provides guidance only and does not include an automated testing tool.
Testing requires written authorization, controlled accounts, and a defined target scope.
Blind, asynchronous, and WebSocket authorization failures may require specialized instrumentation.
UUIDs, session-bound tokens, and rate limits can reduce enumeration coverage.

use_cases.title: Validate Customer Isolation
use_cases.description: Compare controlled accounts to verify that each customer can access only owned profiles, orders, files, and messages.

use_cases.title: Review API Authorization
use_cases.description: Create regression checks for object ownership across read, update, and delete endpoints.

use_cases.title: Teach Access Control
use_cases.description: Demonstrate IDOR discovery and remediation in a laboratory containing synthetic users and records.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an IDOR checklist for my authorized test. Cover URLs, parameters, bodies, files, expected ownership checks, and evidence requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured starting point.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Two-Account Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan non-destructive IDOR tests using two controlled accounts. List requests, identifier changes, expected denials, and safe stopping conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A tester has two accounts in a staging environment.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Captured Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these sanitized request and response descriptions for possible IDOR. Separate confirmed evidence, uncertainty, impact, and recommended validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs help interpreting authorized test results.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Test Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a scoped IDOR matrix across roles, methods, API versions, files, and asynchronous workflows. Include request budgets and non-destructive verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: An application security team is planning broad authorization coverage.

output_examples.input: Plan an authorized two-account review for profile and invoice access.
output: Test each account's own profile and invoice before changing identifiers.
Expect denial when either account requests the other's resources.
Record endpoint, role, object owner, response status, and ownership evidence.
Stop before downloading sensitive content or changing production data.

output_examples.input: Summarize a finding where Account A can view Account B's invoice metadata.
output_examples.output: Confirmed horizontal authorization failure. Account A received Account B's invoice metadata. Restrict queries by authenticated owner and add cross-account regression tests.

output_examples.input: Recommend remediation for an address endpoint that trusts a submitted user identifier.
output_examples.output: Derive the user from the authenticated session. Query the address by both object identifier and owner. Return a consistent denial for mismatches.

best_practices: Use written scope, isolated test accounts, synthetic records, and a fixed request budget.
Prefer non-destructive proof and minimize access to data belonging to other accounts.
Document ownership context, expected denial, actual response, impact, and reproducible remediation tests.
anti_patterns: Do not enumerate production identifiers without explicit limits and monitoring.
Do not bypass rate limits, rotate source addresses, or conceal testing activity.
Do not modify or download real user data when metadata or controlled records can prove the issue.

faq.question: What is IDOR?
faq.answer: IDOR occurs when an application accepts an object reference without verifying that the authenticated user may access that object.

faq.question: Does using UUIDs prevent IDOR?
faq.answer: No. UUIDs reduce predictability, but the server must still enforce authorization for every requested object.

faq.question: Why are two accounts useful?
faq.answer: Two controlled accounts show whether one user can read or change resources owned by another user.

faq.question: Can this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides procedures and examples. A tester must configure tools, define scope, send requests, and review evidence.

faq.question: How should a finding be proven safely?
faq.answer: Use synthetic records and the least sensitive response needed. Avoid state changes unless the environment, scope, and rollback procedure permit them.

faq.question: What is the primary remediation?
faq.answer: Enforce server-side object authorization using the authenticated identity. Filter every lookup and mutation by both object identifier and permitted owner.
